## Definition check

The "Reproducibility" section is present in my instructions and reads as expected of the current rules. The sentence beginning "Repeatability must be", verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

## Evaluation complete

`output_evaluation.json` written and validated: `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic` (exit 0).

**Score: 67 / 88.** No question was excluded, so `excluded_max_points: 0`, `adjusted_max_points: 88`, and both bases coincide at **76.1%** (`fixed_percentage` = `normalized_percentage` = 67/88). `questions_not_applicable: 0`, `excluded_item_ids: []`.

| Category | Score | Max |
|---|---|---|
| Structural Completeness (Q1–5) | 18 | 21 |
| Metadata Quality & Content (Q6–10) | 18 | 21 |
| Technical Documentation (Q11–15) | 16 | 25 |
| FAIRness & Accessibility (Q16–20) | 15 | 21 |

**Applicability.** All four trigger conditions resolved before scoring; every conditional question came out applicable, so there are no `null` scores. Human subjects (gates Q8, Q15) was evidenced from `description`, `keywords` and `collection_mechanisms` — never Q8's or Q15's own fields. Software output (gates Q11) was evidenced from `external_resources` naming the chorus-ai GitHub organization, not from Q11's strategy fields. Datasets-shared (gates Q10, Q17, and with collection Q12/Q13) is approval-gated rather than open, which is exactly the borderline case the ambiguity rule resolves toward `applicable: true`. Each decision is recorded in `applicability_status` and `applicability_evidence`.

**Where semantic analysis moved scores.** Eleven issues detected (14 consistency checks passed, 5 failed, 6 warnings). The two that cost the most: `involves_human_subjects: true` with PICU and NICU cohorts but no named IRB, no approval identifier and no `informed_consent` field at all held Q8 to 3; and the total absence of `version`, `version_access`, `errata`, `doi` and `citation` on a record that labels itself "partially released" and growing put Q13 below the 3 band at 2. Q20 was held at 3 by a consistency failure rather than an absence — `known_limitations.representativeness_limitation` describes a selection bias that `known_biases` does not carry forward. Grant OT2OD032701 validates against the NIH pattern; no DOI or RRID is present; one external resource lacks a URL scheme and the primary maintainer email domain is a misspelling of harvard.edu, so `url_validity` is `some_invalid`.

The record's own `source_caveats` are candid about several of these gaps. I treated that candour as documentation hygiene, which it is, and not as coverage of the missing content, which it is not.
